# Demo video script (~18 min)

The six sections follow the "Demo video requirements" in the assignment, in order. Each step has **Show** (what's on screen), **Run** (commands) and **Say** (talking points; speak them in your own words).

## Before recording (5 min)

```zsh
k3d cluster start urumi            # if the Mac slept
kubectl -n urumi get pods          # all Running, setup Completed
make credentials                   # copy the two passwords into a note
```
**Every login in the demo.** Passwords are random, generated by Helm on first install and kept in Kubernetes Secrets, so they're never in git. Print them with the commands below.

| What | URL | User | Password / key |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gateway dashboard, user A (admin) | http://app.localtest.me | `admin@example.com` | `make admin-password` |
| Gateway dashboard, user B (member) | invite link from Members | `b@example.com` | you set it when accepting the invite |
| WooCommerce admin | http://store.localtest.me/wp-admin | `admin` | `make store-password` |
| Storefront checkout | http://store.localtest.me | none (guest checkout) | none |
| MCP endpoint (Claude Code / Inspector) | http://app.localtest.me/mcp | n/a | B's API key: Dashboard → My API keys, shown once |
| Chat agent LLM | NVIDIA `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` | n/a | your NVIDIA key, already in Secret `urumi-gateway` (`LLM_API_KEY`) |
| Postgres (section 4 queries) | `kubectl exec urumi-postgres-0` | `gateway` | not needed (local socket) |

`make credentials` prints the first and third rows (both dashboards' URLs, users and passwords) in one go.

- Browser window 1: http://app.localtest.me (log in as admin) and http://store.localtest.me.
- Browser window 2: **private/incognito**, for user B.
- A terminal with large font, in the repo folder. Have VS Code open on `apps/gateway/src/core.ts`.
- Optional: in the dashboard, remove leftover test users/keys so lists are short.
- Turn on Do Not Disturb. Zoom the browser to 125%.

## 1. System design and implementation (4 min)

**Show:** the architecture diagram in `docs/design-and-tradeoffs.md`.
**Say:**
- Four layers: the WooCommerce store, my WooCommerce MCP server, the gateway (with dashboard), and the chat agent.
- The gateway is an MCP **server** to clients and an MCP **client** to every registered upstream. Nothing talks to upstreams except the gateway. That's true for the chat agent too.
- Three upstreams: woo-mcp (mine), utils-mcp (mine, bearer-protected), and the official MCP reference server.

**DoD flow live, two users.** Follow this order exactly:

1. **Store.** In window 1: storefront → add *Urumi Mug* to the cart → checkout → **Cash on delivery** → place order. Open WP admin → WooCommerce → Orders and show the order.
2. **User A (admin) in Chat:** *"Create a product called Demo Mug priced 12.50."* Point at the 🔧 `woo__create_product` chip. Refresh the storefront and show it's there.
3. Order the **Demo Mug** on the storefront by hand (COD).
4. **Chat:** *"What orders came in today?"* It returns that order (🔧 `woo__list_orders`).
5. **Invite user B.** Members → invite `b@example.com` → copy the link → open it in window 2 (private) → set a password. As B: **My API keys** → create a key → copy the Claude Code command.
6. **External client as B:**
   ```zsh
   claude mcp add --transport http urumi http://app.localtest.me/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <B's key>"
   claude
   ```
   In Claude Code: `/mcp` shows the tools from all three servers. Ask *"What orders came in today?"*, then *"What's the total of today's orders in EUR?"* (woo + utils, two upstreams in one prompt).
   No Claude Code? Use `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector`: Streamable HTTP, the URL, header `Authorization: Bearer <key>` → List Tools → call `woo__list_orders` with `{"period":"today"}`.
7. **Revoke B's key** (window 1, Members → All API keys → Revoke). In Claude Code, ask again: the call is rejected (401).
8. **Disable a server.** Servers → *Everything* → Disable. Chat: its tools are gone. Claude Code: `/mcp` → reconnect, and the `everything__*` tools are gone.
   *Say:* the gateway is stateless, so it can't push "tools changed". Clients see it when they re-list, and direct calls are refused anyway.
9. **Kill an upstream pod:**
   ```zsh
   kubectl -n urumi scale deploy urumi-utils-mcp --replicas=0
   ```
   Dashboard → Servers: *Utilities* goes **Unreachable** with the reason (`ECONNREFUSED`) within ~10 s. Chat *"what orders came in today?"* still works.
   ```zsh
   kubectl -n urumi scale deploy urumi-utils-mcp --replicas=1     # comes back Connected by itself
   ```
   *(Scaling to 0 keeps it dead long enough to see. `kubectl delete pod` also works, but Kubernetes restarts it in seconds.)*
10. **Audit log** (window 1): every call above, with who, server, tool, time, duration and outcome. Point out B's `denied – API key revoked` row and the `chat` vs `mcp` source column.

## 2. Kubernetes (3 min)

**Run:**
```zsh
kubectl get ns
kubectl -n urumi get deploy,statefulset,svc,ingress,pvc,netpol,secret
kubectl -n urumi describe deploy urumi-gateway | grep -E -A3 "Limits|Requests|Liveness|Readiness"
kubectl -n urumi get secret urumi-gateway -o json | jq '.data | keys'
```
**Say:**
- One namespace `urumi`. StatefulSets for MariaDB and Postgres, each with a PVC. WordPress content is on its own PVC.
- **Public:** only two Ingress hosts, `store.` and `app.`. **Internal:** woo-mcp, utils, everything, both databases: ClusterIP only, no Ingress.
- Every workload has requests, limits, and readiness/liveness probes (startup probes on WordPress/MariaDB for first boot).
- Secrets: generated by Helm on first install and reused on upgrades (`lookup`). In prod they're pre-created (`existingSecret`). Nothing is in git.

**Prove "internal-only" is enforced** (NetworkPolicy, not just "no Ingress"):
```zsh
kubectl -n urumi run probe --rm -i --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl:8.11.1 -- curl -s -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://urumi-woo-mcp:3000/healthz
# → 000 (blocked)
kubectl -n urumi run probe2 --rm -i --restart=Never --labels=app.kubernetes.io/component=gateway --image=curlimages/curl:8.11.1 -- sh -c 'sleep 5; curl -s -m 5 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://urumi-woo-mcp:3000/healthz'
# → 200 (only pods labelled as the gateway get in)
```
*Say:* default-deny ingress. woo-mcp accepts only the gateway, and can itself reach only its WordPress and DNS. utils/everything can reach only DNS. The gateway can't reach the cloud metadata IP.

## 3. MCP internals (3 min)

**Show:** `apps/gateway/src/core.ts` (`listTools`, `callTool`) and `apps/gateway/src/upstream.ts` (`withUpstream`).
**Say, as one trace:** Claude Code → `POST /mcp` with a bearer key → key looked up by prefix, SHA-256 compared → name `woo__list_orders` split at the first `__` → server `woo` loaded (enabled?) → its credential decrypted in memory → short-lived MCP session to `http://urumi-woo-mcp:3000/mcp` with **its own** token → woo-mcp calls WooCommerce REST v3 inside the cluster → result back → audit row written.
- **Collisions:** always `<server>__<tool>`. Show both `utils__echo` and `everything__echo` on the Servers page.
- **Listing:** served from a cache refreshed every 10 s by one replica (Postgres advisory lock). A slow upstream can't slow down `tools/list`.
- **Timeouts:** per server. *Live:* Servers → Utilities → Edit → timeout `2000` → Chat: *"use the utils sleep tool for 5 seconds"* → `timed out after 2000ms`. Set it back to 15000.
- **Dead upstream:** clear error, marked unreachable at once, its tools leave the list, the others are unaffected (you showed this in section 1).

## 4. Security posture (3 min)

**Run** (shows what's stored):
```zsh
kubectl -n urumi exec urumi-postgres-0 -- psql -U gateway -d gateway -c "select slug, auth_type, left(credential_enc, 30) as credential_encrypted from servers"
kubectl -n urumi exec urumi-postgres-0 -- psql -U gateway -d gateway -c "select prefix, left(key_hash, 16) as sha256, revoked_at is not null as revoked from api_keys"
```
**Say:**
- API keys are stored as SHA-256 only and shown once. Revocation is instant and audited.
- Upstream credentials are AES-256-GCM encrypted in Postgres, and the key lives in a Kubernetes Secret. The API is write-only: it returns `hasCredential: true` and never the value. Never sent to the browser or to MCP clients.
- Client tokens are **never** passed through to upstreams (no confused deputy).
- **A member can:** use every enabled tool, see servers and tools, and manage their own keys. **A member can't:** add/edit servers, see URLs or credentials, see others' keys or audit rows. *(Show B's dashboard: no Members page, no "Add server".)*
- **Malicious MCP server:** only admins can add servers. The SSRF guard blocks metadata, private and cluster IPs (*live:* Add server with URL `http://169.254.169.254/` → rejected). Tool names are namespaced, so it can't shadow `woo__*`. Descriptions are capped and labelled with the server. The chat treats tool output as data. It's network-confined. Remaining risk: prompt injection through its outputs. The next step is per-role tool permissions. (See `docs/threat-model.md`.)

## 5. Chat agent (1.5 min)

**Show:** `apps/gateway/src/chat.ts`.
**Say:**
- An OpenAI-compatible tool loop: list the user's tools, call the LLM, run each requested tool **through the same `callTool` as `/mcp`**, feed results back, repeat (max 8 rounds).
- It acts as the logged-in user. Its calls appear in the audit log under that user with source `chat`. The LLM never sees any key.
- The provider is config only: currently NVIDIA `glm-5.3-flash`, and Groq works too. Rate limits are retried after the provider's requested delay.

## 6. Local → VPS (2 min)

**Run:**
```zsh
diff charts/urumi/values-local.yaml charts/urumi/values-prod.yaml
helm history urumi -n urumi
```
**Say:**
- Same charts. Only values differ: the domain (real DNS instead of `localtest.me`), TLS via cert-manager, storage size/class, pre-created Secrets, and 2 gateway replicas with a PodDisruptionBudget.
- k3d locally and k3s on the VPS: the same Traefik, local-path storage and NetworkPolicy engine, so there are no surprises.
- **Upgrade:** new image tag → `helm upgrade` → a rolling update with zero unavailable pods. DB migrations are expand-only, so **rollback** is `helm rollback urumi <revision>`. The store's setup Job re-runs on upgrade and applies the pinned WooCommerce version.
- *(Optional live:* `helm rollback urumi <previous revision> -n urumi` then `helm history` to show the new revision.)*

- CI runs this whole flow on a real k3d cluster on every push (~50 checks), and `scripts/dod.sh` is the curl version of what you just watched.
